clue.text: In flight notice lark

indicators.note: the notice is placed in the word for flight, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a flight from danger is an escape
an ad is a notice, as in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A notice posted on an aircraft about some prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In flight' reads as aboard a plane, but flight here is a running away.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of mischievous fun, the same as an adventurous prank.

clue.text: Sit and adore worked-out body

indicators.note: worked out as in solved or reworked, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to sit and admire someone's gym-toned physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked-out body' suggests a muscular person; the body is a heavenly one.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavenly body is any natural object in space, and a minor planet is one such.

clue.text: I really put the sauce away in elementary form

parts.note: taken as written
so as an intensifier, as in 'so good'
the sauce is slang for alcohol; to tope is to drink it heavily

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to having polished off the gravy in a basic version of a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks culinary but is slang for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Each variety of a chemical element with a different neutron count is one of these forms.

clue.text: Shifty copper turns up in festering hole

indicators.note: the reversed copper symbol goes inside the rearranged letters
something festering is rotting and changing, so the letters of hole are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the symbol bottom to top

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A dodgy policeman appears in a rotten den.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche describes someone disreputable or of dubious character, close to shifty.

clue.text: Gap one found in covering America

indicators.note: the numeral one is found inside the headwear

parts.note: a hat is a covering for the head
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gap discovered in protection for the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a break or pause in continuity, a synonym for a gap.

clue.text: Collection arranged precisely by one in shops

parts.note: just so means neatly arranged, exactly as it should be

indicators.note: the numeral one is put inside the word for shops

parts.note: stores are shops
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Goods neatly laid out by somebody working in retail.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories (1902) is a collection of children's tales on how animals got their features.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's book gathers a series of fables, so it is a collection of tales.

clue.text: Dummy supporting crimes — one adding to distress

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: a job is slang for a crime, as in a bank job
a comforter is a baby's dummy, a rubber teat (a pacifier in US English)

explanation.surface: A baby's pacifier backing up wrongdoing, someone making things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Job, the friends who came to console Job only made his suffering worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a person who, while seeming to console, actually deepens someone's misery.

clue.text: Youngster bound to have smart perception

parts.note: to bound is to leap, as is to spring
chic means stylish or smart
ken is range of knowledge or understanding

explanation.surface: A young person is sure to be sharp and perceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but bound is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually in 'no spring chicken', the phrase means a young person.

clue.text: Wear down a nail point

parts.note: taken as written
a brad is a thin flat-headed nail
E for east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Filing a fingernail tip until it is worn away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nail' suggests a fingernail but is the carpenter's kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or erode by friction, i.e. wear away.

clue.text: Reticent guy backing one short performance

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for guy is read backwards

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a man or fellow
I is the Roman numeral for one
a turn is a short act in a variety show

explanation.surface: A quiet man supports a solo act.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means habitually saying little, synonymous with reserved and reticent.

clue.text: Animal jumping in river with two ducks

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, and two noughts look like the letters

explanation.surface: A creature leaping into a river alongside a pair of waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Ducks are not birds here: in cricket a duck is a zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: A roo is a kangaroo, the hopping marsupial of Australia.

clue.text: Ring company about returning tax book

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the company abbreviation goes about, i.e. around, the reversed tax
returning means the tax word is read backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Phone a firm about a tax refund on a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' reads as telephone, but is just the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An octavo is a book size made by folding sheets into eight leaves, so a type of book.

clue.text: Bumpkin holding hearts in game

indicators.note: the rustic holds the card-suit letter inside him

parts.note: a peasant is an unsophisticated country person
H is the bridge abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A country yokel clutching hearts during a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts and game suggest cards, but game means birds that are shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is wild birds and animals hunted for sport; the pheasant is the classic example.

clue.text: Excellent recital to start with song

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, and the numeral is written as the letter I

indicators.note: only the opening letter of recital is used

parts.note: taken as written; only its opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: An outstanding concert begins with a song.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple tune or melody, so a song.

clue.text: Threatens spirit with death more than once?

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite
an end is a death, and more than one makes it plural

explanation.surface: A spirit repeatedly menaced with dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'death more than once' is a plural of one word for death.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends is about to happen and hangs over one, as a threat does.

clue.text: Creature of habit in conundrum

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of the next word

parts.note: taken as written; the answer is in its middle letters

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in their ways is puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature of habit' is a set phrase for a stick-in-the-mud; here the habit is a religious robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a religious order wears the garment called a habit.

clue.text: Son runs into trap getting minor wound

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the trap word

parts.note: to catch is to trap
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A boy rushes into a snare and comes away grazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a slight skin injury, the mildest kind of wound.

clue.text: Film actors on holiday

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a production
someone away is off on a break

explanation.surface: Performers taking a vacation from a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast Away (2000) is the film in which Tom Hanks is stranded on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a well-known Hollywood movie.

clue.text: CIA battling with triad in the sea

indicators.note: letters in a fight are thrown about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: American spies fighting a Chinese gang out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans.

clue.text: Soy sprinkled on short tailless shellfish

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first
sprinkled letters are scattered, so soy is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: terse means short, curt

explanation.surface: Soy sauce splashed on clipped shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' is not an abbreviation signal; it is a synonym, terse, which then loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are bivalve molluscs, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Witches have a go where cathedral was destroyed

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
to try is to have an attempt

explanation.surface: Witches attempting something where a cathedral was burned.
explanation.walkthrough: Coventry is an English city whose cathedral was bombed in the Blitz in 1940.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in the English Midlands lost its medieval cathedral to wartime bombing.

clue.text: Cereal coating a large upside-down cake

indicators.note: in a down entry, upside-down reads the whole thing bottom to top
the cereal coats, i.e. wraps around, the other two pieces

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cake turned over with a cereal coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upside-down cake' is a familiar dessert, but upside-down is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream, a small cake.

clue.text: Traditional roof in which church?

parts.note: that and which are interchangeable relative pronouns

explanation.surface: A question about which church has an old-style roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed laid as roofing, the old rural method.

clue.text: Old Bob Arnold shortly making snack

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s
Arnie is the short form of the name Arnold

explanation.surface: A man called Bob Arnold briefly preparing a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarnie is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is a light bite eaten between meals or at lunch.

clue.text: Virtuous person imbibing nothing — or their antithesis?

indicators.note: the saint takes in, as if drinking, the round letter

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A teetotal saint, or perhaps a drunk, which is the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint 'imbibing nothing' is sober; the opposite is a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot is a habitual drunkard, the opposite of an abstemious saint.

clue.text: Robust law broken in the beginning

indicators.note: the rearranged law goes inside the beginning word

parts.note: the start is the beginning

indicators.note: a broken law is shattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sturdy legal code breached from the very outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means sturdy and strongly built, like robust.

clue.text: Baked dessert in cold state?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that completes 'baked ___', a meringue-covered ice-cream pudding
second meaning: the chilly northernmost US state

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a partial: baked Alaska is the dessert, so the word alone stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names America's largest, Arctic state and the hot-and-cold pudding with ice cream inside.

clue.text: Check flower for further life?

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a carnation is a garden flower

explanation.surface: Looking over a bloom to see if it will grow again.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born again in a new body after death is a second existence beyond this one.
